requirements.notes: SHA-256 throughout. SHA-1 appears in exactly two protocol-mandated places, TOTP (RFC 6238) and the HIBP k-anonymity range API, both annotated at the import and neither used for a security decision. MD5 has zero occurrences repo-wide.

requirements.requirement: Verify that passwords are stored using an approved, computationally intensive, key derivation function (also known as a "password hashing function"), with parameter settings configured based on current guidance. The settings should balance security and performance to make brute-force attacks sufficiently challenging for the required level of security.
requirements.notes: Argon2id at 46 MiB, 1 iteration, 1 lane, with a 16-byte salt and a server-side pepper.

requirements.requirement: Verify that hash functions used in digital signatures, as part of data authentication or data integrity are collision resistant and have appropriate bit-lengths. If collision resistance is required, the output length must be at least 256 bits. If only resistance to second pre-image attacks is required, the output length must be at least 128 bits.
requirements.notes: SHA-256, 256-bit output.

requirements.requirement: Verify that the application uses approved key derivation functions with key stretching parameters when deriving secret keys from passwords. The parameters in use must balance security and performance to prevent brute-force attacks from compromising the resulting cryptographic key.
requirements.notes: HKDF-SHA256 with domain separation for KEK derivation; Argon2id where the input is a password.

requirements.requirement: Verify that all random numbers and strings which are intended to be non-guessable must be generated using a cryptographically secure pseudo-random number generator (CSPRNG) and have at least 128 bits of entropy. Note that UUIDs do not respect this condition.
requirements.notes: crypto/rand everywhere. math/rand is not imported in any security path.

requirements.requirement: Verify that only approved cryptographic algorithms and modes of operation are used for key generation and seeding, and digital signature generation and verification. Key generation algorithms must not generate insecure keys vulnerable to known attacks, for example, RSA keys which are vulnerable to Fermat factorization.
requirements.notes: Keys are generated by crypto/rsa with the standard library's primality checks.

requirements.requirement: Verify that only the latest recommended versions of the TLS protocol are enabled, such as TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3. The latest version of the TLS protocol must be the preferred option.
requirements.notes: Inbound listeners are TLS 1.3. The Redis client floor is TLS 1.2, which this requirement permits; it is lower because the peer's capability is the operator's, not vault42's.

requirements.requirement: Verify that only recommended cipher suites are enabled, with the strongest cipher suites set as preferred. L3 applications must only support cipher suites which provide forward secrecy.
requirements.notes: TLS 1.3 offers only forward-secret AEAD suites, so the cipher-suite requirement is satisfied by the version pin.

requirements.requirement: Verify that the application validates that mTLS client certificates are trusted before using the certificate identity for authentication or authorization.
requirements.notes: RequireAndVerifyClientCert against a configured CA pool.

requirements.requirement: Verify that TLS is used for all connectivity between a client and external facing, HTTP-based services, and does not fall back to insecure or unencrypted communications.
requirements.notes: The non-dev profile refuses to start without TLS unless an explicit override is set.

requirements.requirement: Verify that external facing services use publicly trusted TLS certificates.
requirements.notes: Certificates are supplied by the operator; the deployment guide requires publicly trusted certificates for the external origin.

requirements.requirement: Verify that an encrypted protocol such as TLS is used for all inbound and outbound connections to and from the application, including monitoring systems, management tools, remote access and SSH, middleware, databases, mainframes, partner systems, or external APIs. The server must not fall back to insecure or unencrypted protocols.
requirements.notes: Outbound SMTP uses net/smtp.SendMail, which negotiates STARTTLS opportunistically with default settings and sets no MinVersion, so it can in principle fall back to plaintext against a hostile or misconfigured relay. The SendGrid path is HTTPS. Compensating controls: mail carries no credential, only single-use links and codes with short expiries; and the NetworkPolicy shipped with the chart restricts SMTP egress to a configured CIDR.

requirements.requirement: Verify that TLS clients validate certificates received before communicating with a TLS server.
requirements.notes: No shipped code sets InsecureSkipVerify, enforced structurally over the whole tree.

requirements.requirement: Verify that TLS or another appropriate transport encryption mechanism used for all connectivity between internal, HTTP-based services within the application, and does not fall back to insecure or unencrypted communications.
requirements.notes: Redis TLS is available and the Postgres DSN defaults to sslmode=require.

requirements.requirement: Verify that TLS connections between internal services use trusted certificates. Where internally generated or self-signed certificates are used, the consuming service must be configured to only trust specific internal CAs and specific self-signed certificates.
requirements.notes: Internal TLS clients validate against the system or operator-supplied trust store; verification is never skipped.

requirements.requirement: Verify that all communication needs for the application are documented. This must include external services which the application relies upon and cases where an end user might be able to provide an external location to which the application will then connect.
requirements.notes: External dependencies (Postgres, Redis, SMTP or SendGrid, OIDC providers) are documented.

requirements.requirement: Verify that communications between backend application components that don't support the application's standard user session mechanism, including APIs, middleware, and data layers, are authenticated. Authentication must use individual service accounts, short-term tokens, or certificate-based authentication and not unchanging credentials such as passwords, API keys, or shared accounts with privileged access.
requirements.notes: Separate database roles (vault_mig, vault_app, vault_admin) with separate credentials, supplied per role.

requirements.requirement: Verify that communications between backend application components, including local or operating system services, APIs, middleware, and data layers, are performed with accounts assigned the least necessary privileges.
requirements.notes: vault_app holds SELECT and INSERT on the audit table and nothing more; migration 002 narrows it further.

requirements.requirement: Verify that if a credential has to be used for service authentication, the credential being used by the consumer is not a default credential (e.g., root/root or admin/admin).
requirements.notes: Every secret is loaded from a file path; no credential has a default value.

requirements.requirement: Verify that an allowlist is used to define the external resources or systems with which the application is permitted to communicate (e.g., for outbound requests, data loads, or file access). This allowlist can be implemented at the application layer, web server, firewall, or a combination of different layers.
requirements.notes: The chart ships a 259-line NetworkPolicy, enabled by default, restricting egress to Postgres, Redis, DNS and SMTP.

requirements.requirement: Verify that the web or application server is configured with an allowlist of resources or systems to which the server can send requests or load data or files from.
requirements.notes: Outbound destinations are the configured issuer, mail relay and cache; the NetworkPolicy enforces the same set at the network layer.

requirements.requirement: Verify that a secrets management solution, such as a key vault, is used to securely create, store, control access to, and destroy backend secrets. These could include passwords, key material, integrations with databases and third-party systems, keys and seeds for time-based tokens, other internal secrets, and API keys. Secrets must not be included in application source code or included in build artifacts. For an L3 application, this must involve a hardware-backed solution such as an HSM.
requirements.notes: Secrets are read from files supplied by the platform secret store, never from source or build artifacts, and byte-typed key material is zeroed on shutdown.

requirements.requirement: Verify that access to secret assets adheres to the principle of least privilege.
requirements.notes: Each process reads only the secrets its role needs; the migration password is not read by the application role.

requirements.requirement: Verify that the application is deployed either without any source control metadata, including the .git or .svn folders, or in a way that these folders are inaccessible both externally and to the application itself.
requirements.notes: The image is built from a scratch-style final stage containing the binary and its static assets only. Test repointed in the register-integrity pass to a case that exercises the clause directly.

requirements.requirement: Verify that debug modes are disabled for all components in production environments to prevent exposure of debugging features and information leakage.
requirements.notes: The default profile is production and an unrecognised profile falls through to production; the dev relaxations are reachable only by naming the dev profile explicitly.

requirements.requirement: Verify that web servers do not expose directory listings to clients unless explicitly intended.
requirements.notes: The static handler serves the SPA entry point and named assets; it produces no directory index.

requirements.requirement: Verify that using the HTTP TRACE method is not supported in production environments, to avoid potential information leakage.
requirements.notes: Go's ServeMux routes by method pattern; TRACE matches no route and returns 405.

requirements.requirement: Verify that documentation (such as for internal APIs) and monitoring endpoints are not exposed unless explicitly intended.
requirements.notes: The metrics endpoint is mounted only when explicitly enabled; the admin plane is a separate binary on loopback behind mutual TLS.

requirements.requirement: Verify that all sensitive data created and processed by the application has been identified and classified into protection levels. This includes data that is only encoded and therefore easily decoded, such as Base64 strings or the plaintext payload inside a JWT. Protection levels need to take into account any data protection and privacy regulations and standards which the application is required to comply with.
requirements.notes: The inventory and its protection levels are documented, and the scrub lists are the executable half.

requirements.requirement: Verify that all sensitive data protection levels have a documented set of protection requirements. This must include (but not be limited to) requirements related to general encryption, integrity verification, retention, how the data is to be logged, access controls around sensitive data in logs, database-level encryption, privacy and privacy-enhancing technologies to be used, and other confidentiality requirements.
requirements.notes: Encryption, retention, logging and access rules are stated per data class.

requirements.requirement: Verify that sensitive data is only sent to the server in the HTTP message body or header fields, and that the URL and query string do not contain sensitive information, such as an API key or session token.
requirements.notes: No credential appears in any route pattern or query string; the OAuth result is delivered in a URL fragment, which is not sent to the server or logged.

requirements.requirement: Verify that the application prevents sensitive data from being cached in server components, such as load balancers and application caches, or ensures that the data is securely purged after use.
requirements.notes: Single-use artifacts are purged atomically as they are read; no plaintext PII is cached.

requirements.requirement: Verify that defined sensitive data is not sent to untrusted parties (e.g., user trackers) to prevent unwanted collection of data outside of the application's control.
requirements.notes: No analytics, tracker or third-party beacon exists. Addresses are pseudonymised before logging.

requirements.requirement: Verify that controls around sensitive data related to encryption, integrity verification, retention, how the data is to be logged, access controls around sensitive data in logs, privacy and privacy-enhancing technologies, are implemented as defined in the documentation for the specific data's protection level.
requirements.notes: Scrubbing, retention and access control are implemented as documented for each class.

requirements.requirement: Verify that authenticated data is cleared from client storage, such as the browser DOM, after the client or session is terminated. The 'Clear-Site-Data' HTTP response header field may be able to help with this but the client-side should also be able to clear up if the server connection is not available when the session is terminated.
requirements.notes: Client-side storage clearing is a property of the browser application, which is assessed separately. vault42's own session cookie is cleared with MaxAge -1 on logout (internal/handler/auth.go:307).

requirements.requirement: Verify that the application sets sufficient anti-caching HTTP response header fields (i.e., Cache-Control: no-store) so that sensitive data is not cached in browsers.
requirements.notes: Cache-Control: no-store and Pragma: no-cache on every API response; only the public metadata documents opt into caching.

requirements.requirement: Verify that data stored in browser storage (such as localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB, or cookies) does not contain sensitive data, with the exception of session tokens.
requirements.notes: The only value vault42 places in browser storage is the session token itself, as a __Host- HttpOnly cookie, which is the exception this requirement allows.

requirements.requirement: Verify that application documentation defines risk based remediation time frames for 3rd party component versions with vulnerabilities and for updating libraries in general, to minimize the risk from these components.
requirements.notes: SECURITY.md states the remediation windows; the nightly scan is the detection mechanism.

requirements.requirement: Verify that an inventory catalog, such as software bill of materials (SBOM), is maintained of all third-party libraries in use, including verifying that components come from pre-defined, trusted, and continually maintained repositories.
requirements.notes: An SBOM is attached to every released image, with build provenance and a cosign signature.

requirements.requirement: Verify that the application documentation identifies functionality which is time-consuming or resource-demanding. This must include how to prevent a loss of availability due to overusing this functionality and how to avoid a situation where building a response takes longer than the consumer's timeout. Potential defenses may include asynchronous processing, using queues, and limiting parallel processes per user and per application.
requirements.notes: Argon2id is the deliberately expensive operation and is documented with its concurrency semaphore.

requirements.requirement: Verify that the application only contains components which have not breached the documented update and remediation time frames.
requirements.notes: Transitive floors are declared as pnpm overrides and asserted against the lockfile; the Go toolchain is pinned.

requirements.requirement: Verify that the application has implemented defenses against loss of availability due to functionality which is time-consuming or resource-demanding, based on the documented security decisions and strategies for this.
requirements.notes: The Argon2id semaphore sheds load with 503 rather than exhausting memory, and request bodies are capped at 8 KiB.

requirements.requirement: Verify that the production environment only includes functionality that is required for the application to function, and does not expose extraneous functionality such as test code, sample snippets, and development functionality.
requirements.notes: Optional surfaces (metrics, OAuth, registration, blobs, KMS) are each mounted only when configured.

requirements.requirement: Verify that the application only returns the required subset of fields from a data object. For example, it should not return an entire data object, as some individual fields should not be accessible to users.
requirements.notes: Responses are explicit view types. The audit fingerprint hash is json:"-" so it cannot leak through a model serialisation.

requirements.requirement: Verify that where the application backend makes calls to external URLs, it is configured to not follow redirects unless it is intended functionality.
requirements.notes: Outbound provider calls target the pinned issuer; the discovery document's issuer is verified rather than followed.

requirements.requirement: Verify that the application has countermeasures to protect against mass assignment attacks by limiting allowed fields per controller and action, e.g., it is not possible to insert or update a field value when it was not intended to be part of that action.
requirements.notes: DisallowUnknownFields on the public API rejects a request carrying a field the handler did not declare, which is the mass-assignment vector. The admin plane decodes without it, which is a lower-severity gap noted for the handoff since the plane is loopback-only behind mutual TLS.

requirements.requirement: Verify that all proxying and middleware components transfer the user's original IP address correctly using trusted data fields that cannot be manipulated by the end user, and the application and web server use this correct value for logging and security decisions such as rate limiting, taking into account that even the original IP address may not be reliable due to dynamic IPs, VPNs, or corporate firewalls.
requirements.notes: The client address is taken from the connection unless a trusted-proxy list is configured, and the forwarded chain is walked from the right to the first untrusted hop.

requirements.requirement: Verify that the application explicitly ensures that variables are of the correct type and performs strict equality and comparator operations. This is to avoid type juggling or type confusion vulnerabilities caused by the application code making an assumption about a variable type.
requirements.notes: Go is statically typed with no coercion; secret comparisons use constant-time equality.

requirements.requirement: Verify that JavaScript code is written in a way that prevents prototype pollution, for example, by using Set() or Map() instead of object literals.
requirements.notes: Prototype pollution is a JavaScript defect class. The Go server has no prototype chain; the browser application is assessed separately.

requirements.requirement: Verify that the application has defenses against HTTP parameter pollution attacks, particularly if the application framework makes no distinction about the source of request parameters (query string, body parameters, cookies, or header fields).
requirements.notes: Parameters are read through net/url and net/http accessors, which take the first value deterministically, and the request bodies are JSON rather than form-encoded.

requirements.chapter: V16 Security Logging and Error Handling
requirements.requirement: Verify that an inventory exists documenting the logging performed at each layer of the application's technology stack, what events are being logged, log formats, where that logging is stored, how it is used, how access to it is controlled, and for how long logs are kept.
requirements.notes: The 40-constant event catalogue, its storage, retention and access control are documented.

requirements.chapter: V16 Security Logging and Error Handling
requirements.requirement: Verify that each log entry includes necessary metadata (such as when, where, who, what) that would allow for a detailed investigation of the timeline when an event happens.
requirements.notes: When, where, who and what on every entry, asserted through the real logger.

requirements.chapter: V16 Security Logging and Error Handling
requirements.requirement: Verify that time sources for all logging components are synchronized, and that timestamps in security event metadata use UTC or include an explicit time zone offset. UTC is recommended to ensure consistency across distributed systems and to prevent confusion during daylight saving time transitions.
requirements.notes: TIMESTAMPTZ storage and a Go time.Time carrying its location, so the instant is unambiguous.

requirements.chapter: V16 Security Logging and Error Handling
requirements.requirement: Verify that the application only stores or broadcasts logs to the files and services that are documented in the log inventory.
requirements.notes: Audit records go to the audit table only; there is no secondary sink.

requirements.chapter: V16 Security Logging and Error Handling
requirements.requirement: Verify that logs can be read and correlated by the log processor that is in use, preferably by using a common logging format.
requirements.notes: Structured rows with typed columns and a JSON metadata field.

requirements.chapter: V16 Security Logging and Error Handling
requirements.requirement: Verify that when logging sensitive data, the application enforces logging based on the data's protection level. For example, it may not be allowed to log certain data, such as credentials or payment details. Other data, such as session tokens, may only be logged by being hashed or masked, either in full or partially.
requirements.notes: Eleven credential key names scrubbed globally and four user-chosen name keys scrubbed on blob events, recursively, without over-scrubbing other classes.

requirements.chapter: V16 Security Logging and Error Handling
requirements.requirement: Verify that all authentication operations are logged, including successful and unsuccessful attempts. Additional metadata, such as the type of authentication or factors used, should also be collected.
requirements.notes: Success and failure are distinct event types with distinct risk tags.

requirements.chapter: V16 Security Logging and Error Handling
requirements.requirement: Verify that failed authorization attempts are logged. For L3, this must include logging all authorization decisions, including logging when sensitive data is accessed (without logging the sensitive data itself).
requirements.notes: Failed admin authentication, lockout and the killswitch trip are all logged, but RBACCheck answers 403 without writing an audit record, so a permission denial leaves no trail. The denial is still enforced; only its observability is missing, and the admin plane is loopback-only behind mutual TLS so the population of possible callers is already small and identified.

requirements.chapter: V16 Security Logging and Error Handling
requirements.requirement: Verify that the application logs the security events that are defined in the documentation and also logs attempts to bypass the security controls, such as input validation, business logic, and anti-automation.
requirements.notes: Rate-limit trips, fingerprint anomalies, replay detection and honeypot triggers are all distinct events.

requirements.chapter: V16 Security Logging and Error Handling
requirements.requirement: Verify that the application logs unexpected errors and security control failures such as backend TLS failures.
requirements.notes: Panics and audit buffer overflow are logged; the drop is counted rather than silent.

requirements.chapter: V16 Security Logging and Error Handling
requirements.requirement: Verify that all logging components appropriately encode data to prevent log injection.
requirements.notes: SafeLogValue neutralises newline, carriage return, tab and null. It does not strip ANSI escapes, which is a terminal-rendering concern rather than a record-forging one; noted for the handoff.

requirements.chapter: V16 Security Logging and Error Handling
requirements.requirement: Verify that logs are protected from unauthorized access and cannot be modified.
requirements.notes: Append-only triggers plus revoked UPDATE and DELETE privileges; the one sanctioned bypass is SECURITY DEFINER with a pinned search_path and EXECUTE revoked from PUBLIC.

requirements.chapter: V16 Security Logging and Error Handling
requirements.requirement: Verify that logs are securely transmitted to a logically separate system for analysis, detection, alerting, and escalation. The aim is to ensure that if the application is breached, the logs are not compromised.
requirements.notes: Audit records live in the same database as the data they describe; there is no shipping to a logically separate system. An adversary with database write access is outside the threat model the append-only triggers defend against, and a hash chain whose signing key lives in the same process would be theatre. Off-box mirroring is a deployment-topology commitment scheduled for 1.1.

requirements.chapter: V16 Security Logging and Error Handling
requirements.requirement: Verify that a generic message is returned to the consumer when an unexpected or security-sensitive error occurs, ensuring no exposure of sensitive internal system data such as stack traces, queries, secret keys, and tokens.
requirements.notes: All 176 server-error responses in the HTTP layer carry fixed message literals, enforced structurally.

requirements.chapter: V16 Security Logging and Error Handling
requirements.requirement: Verify that the application continues to operate securely when external resource access fails, for example, by using patterns such as circuit breakers or graceful degradation.
requirements.notes: Cache loss degrades to a database-backed lockout rather than removing the control, and the credential limiters fail closed.

requirements.chapter: V16 Security Logging and Error Handling
requirements.requirement: Verify that the application fails gracefully and securely, including when an exception occurs, preventing fail-open conditions such as processing a transaction despite errors resulting from validation logic.
requirements.notes: Panics are recovered into a generic 500; critical audit events are exempt from the back-pressure drop.

requirements.requirement: Verify that the Traversal Using Relays around NAT (TURN) service only allows access to IP addresses that are not reserved for special purposes (e.g., internal networks, broadcast, loopback). Note that this applies to both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses.
requirements.notes: vault42 implements no WebRTC signalling, media, or data channels.

requirements.requirement: Verify that the key for the Datagram Transport Layer Security (DTLS) certificate is managed and protected based on the documented policy for management of cryptographic keys.
requirements.notes: vault42 implements no WebRTC signalling, media, or data channels.

requirements.requirement: Verify that the media server is configured to use and support approved Datagram Transport Layer Security (DTLS) cipher suites and a secure protection profile for the DTLS Extension for establishing keys for the Secure Real-time Transport Protocol (DTLS-SRTP).
requirements.notes: vault42 implements no WebRTC signalling, media, or data channels.

requirements.requirement: Verify that Secure Real-time Transport Protocol (SRTP) authentication is checked at the media server to prevent Real-time Transport Protocol (RTP) injection attacks from leading to either a Denial of Service condition or audio or video media insertion into media streams.
requirements.notes: vault42 implements no WebRTC signalling, media, or data channels.

requirements.requirement: Verify that the media server is able to continue processing incoming media traffic when encountering malformed Secure Real-time Transport Protocol (SRTP) packets.
requirements.notes: vault42 implements no WebRTC signalling, media, or data channels.

requirements.requirement: Verify that the signaling server is able to continue processing legitimate incoming signaling messages during a flood attack. This should be achieved by implementing rate limiting at the signaling level.
requirements.notes: vault42 implements no WebRTC signalling, media, or data channels.

requirements.requirement: Verify that the signaling server is able to continue processing legitimate signaling messages when encountering malformed signaling message that could cause a denial of service condition. This could include implementing input validation, safely handling integer overflows, preventing buffer overflows, and employing other robust error-handling techniques.
requirements.notes: vault42 implements no WebRTC signalling, media, or data channels.

requirements.requirement: AAL2: Permitted Authenticator Types
requirements.notes: Password plus a single-factor OTP (TOTP), a multi-factor cryptographic authenticator (WebAuthn), or an out-of-band code.

requirements.requirement: AAL2: Authenticator and Verifier Requirements
requirements.notes: Two distinct authentication factors, each meeting its own section 3 requirements.

requirements.requirement: AAL2: Reauthentication
requirements.notes: Verbatim: "A definite reauthentication overall timeout SHALL be established, which SHOULD be no more than 24 hours at AAL2. The inactivity timeout SHOULD be no more than 1 hour." The SHALL is satisfied: an overall timeout is established and enforced from the family creation instant. Both SHOULDs are not: the default overall timeout is 720 hours rather than 24, and no inactivity timeout exists.

requirements.requirement: General Requirements: Security Controls
requirements.notes: The SP 800-53 control selection is enumerated separately in this register.

requirements.requirement: General Requirements: Privacy Requirements
Password Authenticators
requirements.notes: Subscriber-chosen passwords, no composition rules, no periodic rotation.

requirements.requirement: Password Verifiers
requirements.notes: 15-character minimum for single-factor use, at least 64 permitted, no truncation, Unicode accepted, salted and hashed with Argon2id, 16-byte salt, blocklist by breach corpus.

requirements.requirement: Look-Up Secret Authenticators
requirements.notes: Backup codes generated from crypto/rand with well above 20 bits of entropy.

requirements.requirement: Look-Up Secret Verifiers
requirements.notes: Hashed at rest, single use.

requirements.requirement: Out-of-Band Devices
requirements.notes: Email OTP is bound to the authentication request that produced it and expires. The PSTN is not used.

requirements.requirement: Single-Factor OTP Authenticators
requirements.notes: TOTP seed is at least 128 bits from crypto/rand.

requirements.requirement: Single-Factor OTP Verifiers
requirements.notes: 30-second period, bounded skew, single use, seed encrypted at rest.

requirements.requirement: Multi-Factor Cryptographic Authentication
requirements.notes: WebAuthn/FIDO2, with the authenticator performing activation.

requirements.requirement: Rate Limiting (Throttling)
requirements.notes: Verbatim: the verifier "SHALL limit consecutive failed authentication attempts ... to no more than 100". vault42 locks out at 5 per user in 15 minutes and 20 per IP, with a database-backed fallback if the cache is unavailable.

requirements.requirement: Use of Biometrics
requirements.notes: vault42 operates no biometric verifier. Platform biometrics reach it only through WebAuthn, where the comparison happens on the authenticator and vault42 receives a cryptographic assertion.

requirements.requirement: Attestation
requirements.notes: No authenticator attestation is required or evaluated at enrollment.

requirements.requirement: Phishing Resistance
requirements.notes: WebAuthn provides verifier name binding through the relying-party identifier. It is available, not mandatory, which is what AAL2 permits.

requirements.requirement: Verifier-CSP or IdP Communications
requirements.notes: Authenticated protected channels: TLS 1.3 inbound, pinned issuer and verified JWKS outbound.

requirements.requirement: Replay Resistance
requirements.notes: OTPs, backup codes, reset tokens, authorization codes and refresh tokens are all single use.

requirements.requirement: Authentication Intent
requirements.notes: WebAuthn user presence supplies intent. Recommended rather than required at AAL2.

requirements.requirement: Random Values
requirements.notes: All random values come from an approved DRBG (crypto/rand).

requirements.requirement: Post-Enrollment Binding
requirements.notes: Binding an additional authenticator requires re-confirmation of the existing one.

requirements.requirement: Account Recovery
requirements.notes: Single-use reset tokens; the operator-held escrow requires an offline private key.

requirements.requirement: Expiration
requirements.notes: Authenticators do not expire on a timer; signing keys do, and rotate with an overlap window.

requirements.requirement: Invalidation
requirements.notes: Erasure removes every authenticator; individual factors can be removed after re-confirmation.

requirements.requirement: Account Notifications
requirements.notes: Lockout and credential change both notify the subscriber.

requirements.requirement: Session Bindings: Browser Cookies
requirements.notes: __Host- prefix, HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict.

requirements.requirement: Session Bindings: Access Tokens
requirements.notes: Signed, audience-bound, fingerprint-bound, 15-minute TTL.

requirements.requirement: Reauthentication
requirements.notes: Periodic reauthentication is enforced at the absolute bound but not on inactivity, and the absolute default is well above the AAL2 recommendation. Same finding as 2.2.3.

requirements.requirement: Session Monitoring
requirements.notes: Fingerprint anomalies are detected and audited on every refresh; users can list and revoke their own sessions.

requirements.requirement: Privacy Considerations
Account Management
Access Enforcement
Least Privilege
Unsuccessful Logon Attempts
Device Lock
requirements.notes: Device lock is an endpoint control outside the boundary of a headless authentication server.

requirements.requirement: Session Termination
requirements.notes: Explicit termination is complete and revokes every family, and an absolute age trigger now exists. There is still no inactivity trigger, which is the other half of what this control asks for.

requirements.requirement: Event Logging
requirements.notes: 40 event types covering every selected category.

requirements.requirement: Content of Audit Records
Audit Log Storage Capacity
requirements.notes: Buffer overflow is counted and exempts critical events; retention bounds growth when configured.

requirements.requirement: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
requirements.notes: Records are reviewable through the admin gateway with filtering by user, event type and time window. There is no automated analysis or correlation: risk_score is a hardcoded per-event severity tag that nothing reads, AuditFilter cannot select on it, and no threshold raises an alert.

requirements.requirement: Time Stamps
Protection of Audit Information
requirements.notes: Append-only triggers plus revoked UPDATE and DELETE defeat the realistic adversary, a compromised application role. Cryptographic chaining is absent, so an adversary already holding database write access could rewrite history undetected.

requirements.requirement: Audit Record Retention
Audit Record Generation
Configuration Settings
Identification and Authentication (Organizational Users)
requirements.notes: Admin plane: mutual TLS plus password plus TOTP.

requirements.requirement: Authenticator Management
Authentication Feedback
requirements.notes: Credential failure is generic and constant-time. The four account-state outcomes that once differed by status code (locked, import-claim, banned, disabled) now all answer 401 invalid_credentials without a valid password, closing what was tracked as AR-19 under ASVS V6.3.8.

requirements.notes: Federated login through OIDC providers. Test repointed in the register-integrity pass to a case that exercises the clause directly.

requirements.requirement: Re-authentication
requirements.notes: Re-authentication is required before changes to authentication factors. The separate question of periodic session reauthentication is AC-12 and AR-14.

requirements.requirement: Vulnerability Monitoring and Scanning
requirements.notes: govulncheck, gosec and Trivy run nightly with a HIGH/CRITICAL gate. Test repointed in the register-integrity pass to a case that exercises the clause directly.

Denial-of-service Protection
Boundary Protection

requirements.notes: The old refresh token is invalidated before the replacement is created, so an interrupted rotation fails closed. Previously carried as a partial (OAUTH2-TOKEN-001) on the grounds that the ordering was unverified; it is now asserted.

requirements.notes: HMAC-SHA1 is mandated by the algorithm and is annotated at the import; it is not a free choice of hash. No MD5 exists anywhere in the repository. Test repointed in the register-integrity pass to a case that exercises the clause directly.
